title: Add retention-enforcer RBAC + KMS-tagging migration and audit-sink fanout
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Introduce a retention enforcement service and RBAC bindings to allow automated tombstone of audit records; add a migration to tag existing customer CMKs with region/residency metadata and a safe rollback path; add an audit-sink fanout to the compliance collector. No public API changes; internal infra and policy updates only.
description:
Context and motivation: production retention and key-scoping gaps were identified during a compliance review (ENG-4982). Existing audit logs could be retained beyond policy TTLs due to missing enforcement and operator RBAC guards; similarly, a subset of customer CMKs lacked standardized residency tags which complicates region-aware KMS routing. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) retention-enforcer service and RBAC v2 bindings to manage tombstone jobs, 2) an idempotent KMS tagging migration with verification and rollback, and 3) an audit-sink fanout so compliance consumers (long-term archive, e-discovery, and analytics) receive consistent copies while tombstone runs proceed.

Changes (high-level commits): - Add retention-enforcer microservice + API surface (tombstone scheduler, dry-run mode, metrics) - RBAC policy templates (rbacv2) and a new role: AuditTombstoneOperator scoped to org/tenant boundaries - Migration: kms-tag-migration script (aws/gcp wrappers) with verification hooks and a dry-run flag - Audit sink: fanout adapter to forward canonical audit records to the compliance-collector and s3-archive - Unit + integration tests for policy evaluation and migration safe-paths - Console docs and runbook: how to run migration, roll back, and incident playbook

Files changed (selected): - services/retention-enforcer/main.go (new) - services/retention-enforcer/scheduler.go (new) - infra/rbac/v2/audit_tombstone_role.yaml (new) - tools/migrations/kms_tagging/migrate_tags.py (new) - tools/migrations/kms_tagging/verify.py (new) - observability/metrics/retention_enforcer.prom (new) - api/openapi/retention-enforcer.yaml (new) - docs/rbac/retention-runbook.md (updated) - docs/ops/kms-tagging.md (new) - services/audit-proxy/fanout_adapter.go (updated)

Review conversation: Marcus Lee: "Can the tombstone job be constrained by both tenant and region? We must ensure no cross-region deletion logic." Author: "Yes — the scheduler enforces scope the same way operator role assertions do; tombstone jobs are always evaluated with the request's residency claim and the KMS tag verifier will block deletion for keys missing the matching region tag. Added unit tests to cover multi-tenant scenarios." Priya Patel: "Migration script looks good but we need a way to verify the tags before enabling automatic routing." Author: "Added verify.py and a two-phase migration in the runbook: dry-run -> tag application -> post-verify -> enable routing. The migration supports explicit allowlists for initial rollout." Diego Ramos: "CI flake on integration: kms emulator timeout." Author: "Increased emulator timeouts and added retry on transient errors; re-ran CI." Approvals: Marcus approved after minor comments; Priya approved after runbook additions; Diego approved after CI green.

CI and checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (kms-emulator): initially fail due to timeout, retried, pass - linters: pass - policy-compat-checker: pass - security-scan (deps): warn on one dev dependency (not in production path)

Migration and rollout notes: - Default behavior: migration runs manually via tools/migrations/kms_tagging with --dry-run. - Opt-in: tenant admins can opt-in to automatic tag application per-tenant via the console flag. - Flag gating: the retention-enforcer is deployed disabled by default; enable per-region after migration verification. - Rollback: migration includes a rollback script that unsets tags applied by the run. - Observability: retention-enforcer exposes per-tenant metrics (tombstone_count, dry_run_warning_count, failed_verifications) and audit entries for every deletion.

Security considerations: - New RBAC role (AuditTombstoneOperator) is scoped and requires: operator:region, operator:tenant claims. - KMS tag migration adds no new key material; tags are metadata only. Scripts follow least privilege: separate IAM role for tag writes with allowlist. - Audit-sink fanout preserves canonical audit envelopes and signs forwarded copies to prevent tampering.

Testing performed: end-to-end staging run with synthetic tenants (3 tenants across 2 regions), ran full migration in dry-run and verified no tombstones were scheduled until tags were verified. Load test of tombstone scheduler at 10k records/minute sustained under SLOs.

Merge outcome: squash and merge on 2024-11-20. Notes: tagged as release-note:infra and rolled out to staging immediately; production rollout planned after compliance signoff and an operator training session.
